findings.where: Article page specimen, the pull quote “Whichever PPP Law I am currently working on with a client country!” (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The pull quote is set in logo blue. The palette gives blue three jobs: the wordmark, links and the one button. Here a static line takes it, so blue no longer means 'you can act on this'. On the article page the largest blue text is a quote that does nothing, and it sits just above the underlined blue link to the lecture PDF, which does.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank reader on an article page, who sees large blue text and may take it for a link, and who then has less reason to trust that blue means 'click'. Angélique also objects: when she adds posts she would have no rule for when blue is allowed, and this tile is meant to give her one.

findings.where: Palette, the Mist swatch (#F3F6F9), and the Mist panel standing in for the portrait in the hero (desktop right column, phone below the button)
findings.fault: Mist is listed in the palette, but its only job is 'the portrait stand-in'. Once Mark's photograph arrives, Mist has no job left. The tile still hands it on as a site colour, and it is a cool blue-tinted grey on a palette that is otherwise true white and neutral greys.
findings.who_objects: The designer of the layout round, who is told to work inside this tile. They would get a tinted surface colour with no role, and might use it for panels, which v5 rules out ('nothing in a panel').
